overview.about: World Reef Day is an annual call to action to protect the world's coral reefs - among the most biodiverse and threatened ecosystems on Earth. It encourages individuals, businesses and communities to make choices that reduce the pressure on reefs.
overview.nextEvent: The next World Reef Day is marked on 1 June with awareness campaigns, education and conservation drives. It focuses attention on coral bleaching, ocean warming and the everyday choices that affect reef health.

@graph.name: World Reef Day
@graph.description: World Reef Day is an annual awareness day for coral reefs and the choices that affect them, from warming seas and pollution to tourism and sunscreen use. Reefs support marine biodiversity, fisheries and coastal communities, yet they are highly sensitive to heat stress and declining water quality. The day is most useful when it leads to specific, evidence-based action: follow local reef rules, choose operators with responsible practices, reduce pollution that reaches the sea and learn how a nearby reef is monitored. Australia provides a strong location link because the Great Barrier Reef is the world’s largest coral reef system, but the observance is relevant to reef communities across the tropics.

exploreIntro: These are reef destinations, not host countries: Australia links to the Great Barrier Reef, Belize to its UNESCO-listed barrier reef, and the Philippines to the remote Tubbataha marine park.
participationIntro: Make the day about reef protection and ocean habits:

participationSteps.text: Learn or share one practical reef-protection action, such as reducing pollution, choosing reef-safe travel behaviour or cutting unnecessary waste.
Use the day to highlight coral reefs, marine biodiversity and the pressure reefs face from warming seas.
Join or promote a beach, river or community cleanup if one is available nearby.
If you dive, snorkel or travel, check local reef guidelines before entering the water.
